subject.title: iOS/macOS app cannot connect to a Gateway behind a Basic-auth reverse proxy

question: Should macOS adopt the same per-gateway custom-header contract as iOS/Android, and where should those proxy credentials live in macOS settings/storage?
rationale: The low-level shared header seam exists, but macOS still needs a credential-bearing UI/storage contract that runs before Gateway auth and affects a security boundary.

options.title: Implement Keychain-backed macOS parity
options.body: Use the existing shared sanitizer/TLS-only upgrade path and add macOS secure storage plus settings UI scoped per gateway.

options.title: Limit macOS to typed Basic/Bearer fields
options.body: Expose narrower proxy-auth fields instead of arbitrary headers, reducing flexibility but shrinking the credential surface.

options.title: Defer macOS proxy credentials
options.body: Keep macOS authenticated-proxy support unsupported for now and document VPN, Tailscale, SSH tunnel, or proxy-bypass alternatives.

recommendation.title: Implement Keychain-backed macOS parity
recommendation.body: Use the existing shared sanitizer/TLS-only upgrade path and add macOS secure storage plus settings UI scoped per gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the landed iOS custom-header implementation and has the clearest recent history across this security/product boundary.
